Graph transformer layer with structural attention bias

Source: R/graph-transformers.R
graph_transformer_layer.Rd

Full multi head self attention among the nodes of each graph (never across graphs of a batch), with a learned scalar bias per head for every shortest path distance, as in Graphormer (Ying et al. 2021). Uses the pre-layer-norm arrangement: \(h = h + \mathrm{MHA}(\mathrm{LN}(h))\), then \(h = h + \mathrm{FFN}(\mathrm{LN}(h))\).

Usage

graph_transformer_layer(dim, heads = 4L, max_dist = 5L, dropout = 0.1)

Arguments

dim

Feature size.

heads

Attention heads (dim must be divisible by heads).

max_dist

Largest distinguished distance.

dropout

Dropout probability.

Value

An nn_module called as layer(x, batch, dist) where dist is a B by L by L long tensor of clipped distances (padding uses max_dist + 2).

Details

Graphormer's edge encoding along shortest paths is not implemented. Memory is \(O(B L^2 H)\) for B graphs of at most L nodes and H heads, so this layer suits small graphs such as molecules; for large graphs use the sparse transformer_conv().

The layer is permutation equivariant: distances and attention are functions of node pairs, not of node order.
